item.description:
In previous article, we talked about how the CSV format represents tabular data, its simplicity, and its limitation on data types support. For now, our example still looks similar to regular CSV tutorials because we worked with standard, simplified data. We will dive into complex cases in future articles, and this post will focus on CSV structure: how the format accuratly defines table cells/columns.

item.title: Data Exchange Format (1) - Working with CSV, Part 1
item.dc:creator: Po-Yu Hsieh
item.description:
CSV (Comma-Separated Values) files are common to anyone working with tabular data, no matter if those data are called "tables" or "spreadsheets" in conversations or your computer. If you work in information technology industry, you've likely encountered them repeatedly in class assignments, personal projects, or data-centered tasks in the workplace, from fundamental data engineering to analytics applications.
